subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should unconfigured memory_search enable a periodic interval fallback by default to protect against silent watcher outages, or should periodic sync remain opt-in?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but changing the default affects existing users' background filesystem scans and possible embedding/provider work, which is a product and upgrade-compatibility decision rather than a purely mechanical fix.

options.title: Default periodic fallback after review
options.body: Accept a default-on interval fallback, merge the linked PR after its scoped code review blockers are resolved, and document explicit intervalMinutes: 0 as the opt-out.

options.title: Keep fallback opt-in
options.body: Leave intervalMinutes defaulting to 0 and rework the fix into docs, doctor guidance, or an explicit opt-in recovery path.

options.title: Require live outage proof first
options.body: Pause the default decision until maintainers have a long-running gateway or Crabbox reproduction that shows a real watcher outage and recovery behavior.

recommendation.title: Default periodic fallback after review
recommendation.body: Accept a default-on interval fallback, merge the linked PR after its scoped code review blockers are resolved, and document explicit intervalMinutes: 0 as the opt-out.

likelyOwner.reason: This is closest to the original memory search feature and memory-core owner-boundary history, and it requires a product/default decision rather than only a code repair.
